description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and accuracy (ACC, y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to approximately 10⁴ using a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 80% in linear increments of 5%, with gridlines at each 5% interval. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) shows a steady increase from ~61% at co-occurrence 1 to ~67% at 10⁴. “FT” (blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers) rises from ~62.5% to ~68.5%. “IKE” (red line with upward-pointing triangle markers) starts at ~64.5% and reaches ~70%. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~66.5% and plateaus near 74% after 10². “MEMIT” (purple line with circle markers) starts at ~66.5% and gradually climbs to ~72.5%. “ROME” (green line with square markers) starts at ~72.5% and rises to ~77.5% by 10², then remains nearly flat through 10⁴. All lines exhibit upward trends with diminishing returns at higher co-occurrence numbers, and ROME consistently outperforms the others across the full range.
